Subject: Governance blockers & Q4 delivery plan for Acme - triage

Sara / Acme team —

Thanks again for the detailed security checklist you sent over. Before our next exec sync I want to align internal owners on the remaining blockers so we can give a concrete commitment to Acme about timelines and scope. Top items called out by Acme:

- Audit log fields and retention (granularity + export APIs)
- Data retention policies per-customer and automated purge
- BYOK/KMS integration for key custody and PRD rotation requirements
- SSO SAML + provisioning + SCIM gaps

Neha — can you and Mina triage the technical gaps and note any must-haves vs. nice-to-haves? Laura — can you map these to product workstreams (Console, API, and Private deployment) and call out dependencies on infra (Vivek)?

Acme requested a C-level timeline by Monday 11/23. I know that’s tight, but we should at least provide: 1) list of deliverables we can commit to by EOY Q4, 2) items requiring a Dedicated/Private offering or contract amendment, and 3) showstoppers that block go-live.

I attached Acme's KMS requirements they sent. I’ll consolidate replies into a single plan with ownership.

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Governance blockers & Q4 delivery plan for Acme - triage

Marcus —

Quick initial triage below after a run through the attachment. High level: nothing is impossible, but there are three items that need cross-team alignment and one that will require contract-level approval.

1) Audit logs: we currently emit request-level traces, inference token counts, model id, route, and client id. Missing from their list: per-call metadata (caller resource id), user-supplied labels, and export-friendly CSV schema. Work required: 2 sprint effort to extend logging schema + 1 sprint to add export job and retention controls in Console.

2) Data retention: we support per-customer TTL on embeddings and cache purge, but not automated document-level purge tied to a schedule and legal hold. That needs infra work for index-level purging and UI in Console. 3 sprints with priority queueing.

3) BYOK/KMS: we support provider-managed KMS today (cloud keys). BYOK with external HSM + rotation APIs is larger — requires security review and dedicated key import pipeline. This is a contract-impacting ask (legal & compliance to sign off). Estimate: PoC in 6-8 weeks if we allocate a dedicated infra/security engineer and sign an MSA addendum.

4) SSO/SCIM: basic SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are in our backlog. SAML is near-term (1 sprint to finish tests and docs). Full SCIM + user groups sync + provisioning quirks (Acme uses nested groups) will be 2 sprints.

Open questions for Acme (to resolve priority):
- Which audit fields are mandatory vs optional? (See attached requested_audit_fields.csv)
- Are they OK with a phased BYOK delivery (vaulted keys initially, HSM later)?

I’ll sync with Vivek on infra concurrency impact and with Legal on the BYOK contract language.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor | Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Governance blockers & Q4 delivery plan for Acme - triage

Adding product perspective and rough priorities.

Console/API workstreams (rough split):
- Logging schema + export: Console + Jobs API — medium effort (2 sprints). Candidate for canary in Dedicated customers first.
- Retention scheduling & legal hold: Console + Indexing infra — larger (3 sprints). Can scope MVP to: per-customer TTL + manual legal hold removal.
- BYOK: surface in Console key management page + API for rotation. Dependent on infra security work — can do UI/UX in parallel but backend PoC required.
- SSO/SCIM: SAML finish + SCIM full provisioning (SCIM 1.1 compliance) — SAML short, SCIM medium.

Constraints & notes:
- Dedicated/Private customers get priority for BYOK and retention SLA features (because of data isolation & contract). If Acme requires on-prem HSM we should treat that as Private deployment work.
- Roadmap window: we are currently committing 2 sprints of infra/security capacity to enterprise requests in Dec — if we approve that, we can hit a partial BYOK PoC by mid-Jan.

I recommend we provide Acme with a phased commitment:
A) By 12/31: SAML completion, logging schema extension, export job MVP (export to S3/CSV), and clear list of audit fields delivered.
B) By 1/31: Retention scheduling MVP and BYOK PoC (cloud-KMS import + rotation API).
C) BYOK HSM import + legal sign-off: separate track dependent on contract changes (timeline TBD).

I’ll prepare a short one-pager for Exec that maps these deliverables to sprint counts and owners.

—Laura
Laura Bennett | VP Product Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick triage. Acme's priority order is: 1) BYOK (HSM import is a hard preference), 2) audit fields & export, 3) retention scheduling, 4) SSO gaps (SAML first). Procurement needs estimates for when BYOK HSM work will start for contract language.

We can accept a phased approach (cloud-KMS PoC then HSM) as long as the contract calls out timelines and rollback mitigations. Also attaching our SOC2 summary and example key rotation policy for your reference.
